newsitem.title: UK: P&U says more jobs to go.
newsitem.headline: P&U says more jobs to go.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said on Tuesday it would give an indication of the progress of its latest restructuring and associated savings and costs in the fourth quarter.

In a telephone conference with journalists, newly-appointed president and chief executive officer Fred Hassan said an "indication on progress and the long-term cost-savings and one-time costs through restructuring" would be given in the quarter, with some details available with third-quarter results.
The company also said the restructuring would result in further job losses in addition to the 4,100 positions cut since it was formed through merger.
Chief financial officer Bob Salisbury told Reuters the company would take further action to alter its cost structure.
"It is going to be necessary to take some extraordinary restructuring charges," he said, adding "it will probably result in some workforce reductions.
But Salisbury said there was "no accurate assessment of the number of jobs" likely to be affected.
Hassan, who was appointed to lead the group in May, said he had an "unvarnished" view of the company, which was clearly underperforming.
"I am committed to stabilising and then reversing the negative trend we are seeing (in sales and profits). This is achievable," he said.
Hassan, who moved to P&U from American Home Products Corp, said he would introduce the "rigorous control systems" of his former employer.

Repeating his belief that 1998 would be a year of turnaround, he set particular store by incontinence drug Detrusitol, currently being considered by regulators in the U.S. and Europe. The company is gearing up to start selling the product next year.
Noting that seven million people in the U.S. suffered from urinary incontinence, Hassan said Detrusitol was in a market with no real competitors.
"We haven't had a product like Detrusitol in our pipeline for a long time," Hassan told journalists.
Other new products singled out as engines of future growth were glaucoma drug Xalatan, now being rolled out in the US Europe and South America.
Hassan said he was also optimistic about prospects for a higher strength version of over-the-counter hair loss treatment Rogaine, recently approved in the U.S.
"We hope to launch later this year and get three years' exclusivity," said Hassan.
In the pipeline Hassan singled out new antibiotics, which he said were "the first new class in clinical development for 15 years."
